notes.text: Come up to the mount and be there — Expect to continue there for some time.

Joshua was his minister or servant, and it would be a satisfaction to him to have him with him as a companion during the six days that he tarried in the mount before God called to him. Joshua was to be his successor, and therefore thus he was honoured before the people, and thus he was prepared by being trained up in communion with God. Joshua was a type of Christ, and (as the learned Bishop Peirson well observes Moses takes him with him into the mount, because without Jesus, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, there is no looking into the secrets of heaven, nor approaching the presence of God.

A cloud covered the mount six days — A visible token of God's special presence there, for he so shews himself to us, as at the same time to conceal himself from us, he lets us know so much as to assure us of his power and grace, but intimates to us that we cannot find him out to perfection. During these six days Moses staid waiting upon the mountain, for a call into the presence- chamber. And on the seventh day - Probably the sabbath-day, he called unto Moses. Now the thick cloud opened in the sight of all Israel, and the glory of the Lord broke forth like devouring fire.

Moses went into the midst of the cloud — It was an extraordinary presence of mind, which the grace of God furnished him with, else he durst not have ventured into the cloud, especially when it broke out in devouring fire. And Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights - It should seem the six days, were not part of the forty; for during those six days, Joshua was with Moses, who did eat of the manna, and drink of the brook mentioned, Deut. ix, 21, and while they were together, it is probable Moses did eat and drink with him; but when Moses was called into the midst of the cloud, he left Joshua without, who continued to eat and drink daily while he waited for Moses's return, but from thenceforward Moses fasted. At this chapter begins an account of the instructions God gave Moses for erecting and furnishing the tabernacle. Here are, I. Orders given for a collection to be made among the people, ver. 1-9. II. Particular instructions,

glossa.text:
*Come up to me,* etc. *(BED., lib. I de Tabernac., cap. 11, tom. II.)* Being about to speak of the figure of the tabernacle, etc., *as far as* that the Church might be designated as about to speak throughout the world with the tongues of all nations.

*And I will give thee.* ((ID.)) Like to this is that: *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you ((Matth. XXVIII))*. Therefore neither Moses, nor the apostles, nor anyone whatever, ought to teach other things than those which the Lord taught and prescribed by the decree of his counsel to be observed, in which he willed that we should have eternal life; and just as nothing of these ought to be passed over, so it is needful to commit to the hearers all things which he commanded.

*Moses and Josue rose up. ((AUG., quaest. 103 in Exod.))* Josue, not mentioned among those four, suddenly appears with Moses, etc., *as far as* that at the time now recorded he was not yet called Jesus, but when it was written.

((BED.)) Josue signifies Christ in name and in action; who is called the minister of Moses, because Christ *came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil ((Matth. V))*. He follows the footsteps of Moses in all things, because in all that Moses wrote he is typically designated, and, as an inseparable companion, is found if he be rightly sought. Whence John V: *If you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also.*

((BED., de Tabernac., lib. I, cap. 1, tom. II.)) Aaron ( אהרן ) is interpreted *the mountain of strength,* Hur ( חור ) *fire* or *light,* etc., *as far as* and the mind burns toward the love of the Creator.
*And when Moses was gone up, ((BEDA., ibid.))* As the mountain the height of perfection, etc., *as far as* he protects with heavenly blessing.

*And the glory of the Lord dwelt. ((ID., ibid.))* Not the loftiness only, but the very name of the mountain, etc., *as far as* on the seventh we are bidden to rest.

*Covering it with a cloud. ((ID., ibid.))* For six days he is covered with the cloud and with the glory of the Lord, etc., *as far as* that he might come through to the loftier gifts of the divine vision and converse.
*And the appearance was,* etc. ((ID., ibid.)) The appearance of the glory of the Lord appeared as a burning fire, etc., *as far as* although they are not able to follow them fully.

*And Moses entering in,* etc. ((ID., ibid.)) Moses, having entered the midst of the cloud, went up into the mountain, etc., *as far as* that by the observance of them they may come to eternal salvation.

notes.text: Heathen — Who did so against David, 2 Sam. v, 6, 17; 1 Chron. xiv, 8, and against Christ, Luke xviii, 32 Acts iv, 25, &c.

The kings — Herod, and Pilate and others with or after them. Earth - So called in way of contempt and to shew their madness in opposing the God of heaven. Set - The word denotes the combination of their counsels and forces. Anointed - Against the king whom God hath chosen and exalted.
And cast — The same thing expressed with more emphasis. Let us not only break off their yoke and the cords by which it is fastened upon us, but let us cast them far away.

Sitteth — As the king of the whole world. Heavens - As an evidence both of God's clear and certain knowledge of all things that are done below, and of his sovereign and irresistible power. Laugh - Shall despise them and all their crafty devices.

Yet — Notwithstanding all their artifices and combinations. My king - Who ruleth in my stead, and according to my will, and for my glory. Zion - Over my church and people. Zion strictly taken, was an hill on the north part of Jerusalem, where there was a strong fort, called the city of David, but in a more large sense it is put for the city of Jerusalem, for the temple of Jerusalem, built upon the hill of Moriah, which was either a part of mount Sion, or adjoining to it; for the church of the Jews, and for the Christian church.

The decree — The will and appointment of God concerning this. My son - Which tho' it may in some sort be said to, or of David, yet much more properly belongs to Christ, who is commonly known by this title both in the Old and New Testament, and to whom this title is expressly appropriated by the holy ghost, who is the best interpreter of his own words, Acts xiii, 33 Heb. i, 5. This day - This may be understood either,

1. Of his eternal generation. This day, from all eternity, which is well described by this day, because in eternity there is no succession, no [yesterday,] no [tomorrow,] but it is all as one continued day or moment without change or flux; or,

2. Of the manifestation of Christ's eternal son-ship in time; which was done both in his birth and life, when his being the son of God was demonstrated by the testimony of the angel, Luke i, 32, and of God the Father, Matt. iii, 17; xvii, 5, and by his own words and works; and in his resurrection, which seems to be here mainly intended, of which day this very place is expounded, Acts xiii, 33. When Christ was in a most solemn manner declared to be the son of God with power, Rom. i, 4.
Earth — Not only the Jewish nation, but the whole world.

Them — Those that will not quietly submit to thee, shall be crushed and destroyed by thee. This was in part fulfilled, when the Jews who persisted in unbelief, were destroyed by the Roman power: And in the destruction of the Pagan power, when the Christian religion came to be established. But it will not be compleatly fulfilled, 'till all opposing power and principality be put down.
Now — While you have time for repentance and submission.

Fear — With an awful sense of his great and glorious majesty. Rejoice - Do not esteem his yoke your dishonour and grievance; but rejoice in this inestimable grace and benefit. Trembling - This is added to warn them of taking heed that they do not turn this grace of God into wantonness.

Kiss — In token of your subjection and adoration; whereof this was a sign among the eastern nations. The son - The son of God. Ye perish - Be taken out of the way by death or destruction. Wrath - The least degree of his anger is terrible. David complains to God of his enemies, ver. 1, 2. Comforts himself in God, and the experience of his goodness, ver. 3-6. Triumphs in the salvation of God, ver. 7, 8 A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.

glossa.text: « Why have the nations raged, etc. » ((CASS.)) This psalm is the second in order, the first in title; whence in the Acts of the Apostles it is called the first. First he rebukes the persecutors and threatens them, and foretells as a prophet. « Vain things. » ((Ibid.)) To hold him in death; or, that the world should not go away after him.

« Kings. » ((Ibid.)) The former, who slew the infants, is Herod, the latter, he who consented with Pilate in the death of Christ. Kings and princes. ((Ibid.)) He could also, according to Ambrose, speak in the plural of one man. For only king Herod and prince Pilate are shown by the voice of Peter, in the Acts of the Apostles, to have conspired against Christ.

« Let us break asunder. » ((AMB.)) Or they came together, saying: Let us break asunder their reasonings, that is, of the Lord and of his Christ, or of Christ and of the disciples, by which they wish to bind us to themselves. ((AUG.)) And although it might be said otherwise, it fits more openly those who are unwilling that the yoke of Christ be laid upon them. « Bonds. » The promises of eternal life, and the threatenings of hell, by which they wish to subjugate us to themselves. « Let us cast away. » Their reasonings being destroyed, let us shake off his dominion from us. ((Ibid.)) The yoke, that is, the law: but « he that dwelleth in the heavens. »

« He shall laugh them to scorn. » ((Ibid.)) As when he rose again with the guards set: « He shall deride, » when they were scattered through the world. The derision of God is the force of the foreknowledge which God gives to his saints, that, seeing the name of Christ to be in all nations hereafter, they may understand that those men meditated vain things.

« He shall speak to them. » ((Ibid.)) He opens it more plainly when he says, he shall trouble them. The anger of God is a motion that arises in a soul which knows the law of God, when it sees that law passed over by an evil man, through which motion many things are avenged: or, the anger of God is the darkening of the mind of the transgressors of the law.

« But I. » ((CASS.)) Secondly, he brings in his words concerning his almighty kingdom and his unspeakable generation, where we learn of his divinity and his humanity. « King. » ((ID.)) So also are the kings of the earth appointed by him. « Preaching upon Sion, » so also are the prophets, « The Son, » so also is Israel, « I have begotten thee. » This to Christ alone.

« The Lord hath said. » The person of him that reigns. « My Son. » ((AUG.)) Therefore do I give thee the nations for an inheritance rather than to any obedient servant: because thou art Son by nature, and consubstantial by an ineffable begetting. « This day. » ((Ibid.)) Although it might be taken of the day on which he was born according to man, yet, since "this day" signifies a presence, let it be taken of the everlasting generation of the wisdom of God.

« Ask. » ((AUG.)) It pertains to the taking up of man: which was done for the salvation of men, and according to which he intercedes for us. « An inheritance. » ((CASS.)) Inheritance is from lord (herus), because in it he holds dominion with free power.

« Thou shalt rule them. » ((AUG.)) Partly thou shalt rule, partly thou shalt break, according to that word: « Behold, this one here is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many ((Luc. II)), » so that he who is just may be justified still: and he who is in filth shall be defiled still ((Apoc. XXII)). » « A rod of iron. » ((CASS.)) The power of Christ is the rod of iron; the sinner is the potter's vessel, which is both of clay and easily broken.

« And now, ye kings, understand. » Now, that is, by the things that have been said. ((CAS.)) Thirdly, on account of these things laid open, he admonishes all to obey humbly, and persuades them from the useful, that they perish not, and from the honourable, because blessed are they that trust in him. In this, after Christ, he speaks as it were an Apostle.

((AUG.)) Or, now that I am appointed king, be not sorrowful, ye kings of the earth; for it is expedient for you to be under him, from whom come understanding and learning, that you may not rule rashly, but may serve the Lord of all, and may exult in blessedness.

« Lest at any time he be angry. » ((Ibid.)) The doubt is not according to the prophet, but according to those men themselves, who think upon the anger of God with doubting. « From the just way, » that is, being taken away from Christ, or from good working.

« When his wrath shall be kindled. » ((CASS.)) Now he does not burn when he chastises, as a father, but in the time to come he will burn, because there will be nothing of patience in the time to come. « In a short time his anger. » Because he examines not each of these things separately, but all of them together.

notes.text: These things are worthy to be always had in remembrance For they are not cunningly devised fables — Like those common among the heathens. While we made known to you the power and coming - That is, the powerful coming of Christ in glory. But if what they advanced of Christ was not true, if it was of their own invention, then to impose such a lie on the world as it was, in the very nature of things, above all human power to defend, and to do this at the expense of life and all things only to enrage the whole world, Jews and gentiles, against them, was no cunning, but was the greatest folly that men could have been guilty of. But were eyewitnesses of his majesty - At his transfiguration, which was a specimen of his glory at the last day.

For he received divine honour and inexpressible glory — Shining from heaven above the brightness of the sun. When there came such a voice from the excellent glory - That is, from God the Father. Matt. xvii, 5.
And we — Peter, James, and John. St. John was still alive. Being with him in the holy mount - Made so by that glorious manifestation, as Mount Horeb was of old, Exod. iii, 4, 5.

And we — St. Peter here speaks in the name of all Christians. Have the word of prophecy - The words of Moses, Isaiah, and all the prophets, are one and the same word, every way consistent with itself. St. Peter does not cite any particular passage, but speaks of their entire testimony. More confirmed - By that display of his glorious majesty. To which word ye do well that ye take heed, as to a lamp which shone in a dark place - Wherein there was neither light nor window. Such anciently was the whole world, except that little spot where this lamp shone. Till the day should dawn - Till the full light of the gospel should break through the darkness. As is the difference between the light of a lamp and that of the day, such is that between the light of the Old Testament and of the New. And the morning star - Jesus Christ, Rev. xxii, 16. Arise in your hearts - Be revealed in you.

Ye do well, as knowing this, that no scripture prophecy is of private interpretation — It is not any man's own word. It is God, not the prophet himself, who thereby interprets things till then unknown.

For prophecy came not of old by the will of man — Of any mere man whatever. But the holy men of God - Devoted to him, and set apart by him for that purpose, spake and wrote. Being moved - Literally, carried. They were purely passive therein.

glossa.text:
*For not unlearned fables,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Here he touches both the pagans and the heretics. The pagans feared not to call gods whatsoever delighted them. The heretics, having received the mysteries of the true God, thereafter were zealous not to attend to the divine Scriptures, but rather to transfer them by ill interpretation to an erroneous sense.

*But made beholders,* etc. The transfiguration of the Lord and his brightness was a sign of his resurrection and of ours. By Elias, who appeared with him, is understood the resurrection of those who were before the law. By Moses, that of those who were under the law; by Peter, and James, and John, that of those who are under grace. Or, by Moses dead, that of the dead; by the living, that of the living.

*And we have the more firm.* What I have said to you is not fabulous, but certain, and not only declared by these signs, but also for the confirmation of our preaching we have the prophetic word of David: *The Lord said to me, Thou art my Son ((Psal. II))*, etc., more firm among the other prophets, because he prophesied of Christ more clearly than the others.

*Whereunto you do well to attend. ((BEDA.))* That you may be able to have the light of knowledge, etc., *as far as* in comparison with the life to come we have need of a lamp.

*Understanding this first.* Attend to the prophetic word, for it is from God. Which can be proved by this, that prophecy is not written in such words and in such a manner of speech as men use in their own speech, and as secular writings are composed and interpreted. And truly the utterance of the prophets is not according to their own will, or that of the hearers, but according to the will of the Holy Spirit who was speaking in them.

*For not by human will. ((BEDA.))* As it was not in the power of the prophets always to have the spirit, always to foretell things to come: so it was not of their power that they should teach whatsoever things they would, but they spoke those things alone which they had learned from the spirit. These things are therefore said, lest anyone expound the Scriptures according to his own pleasure.

notes.text: A high mountain — Probably Mount Tabor. Mark ix, 2; Luke ix, 28.

And was transfigured — Or transformed. The indwelling Deity darted out its rays through the veil of the flesh; and that with such transcendent splendour, that he no longer bore the form of a servant. His face shone with Divine majesty, like the sun in its strength; and all his body was so irradiated by it, that his clothes could not conceal its glory, but became white and glittering as the very light, with which he covered himself as with a garment.

There appeared Moses and Elijah — Here for the full confirmation of their faith in Jesus, Moses, the giver of the law, Elijah, the most zealous of all the prophets, and God speaking from heaven, all bore witness to him.
Let us make three tents — The words of rapturous surprise. He says three, not six: because the apostles desired to be with their Master.
Hear ye him — As superior even to Moses and the prophets. See Deut. xviii, 17.
Be not afraid — And doubtless the same moment he gave them courage and strength.

Tell the vision to no man — Not to the rest of the disciples, lest they should be grieved and discouraged because they were not admitted to the sight: nor to any other persons, lest it should enrage some the more, and his approaching sufferings shall make others disbelieve it; till the Son of man be risen again - Till the resurrection should make it credible, and confirm their testimony about it.

glossa.text:
*And after days,* etc. Mark says the same, but Luke eight. These therefore set down the middle days, Luke adds, etc., *as far as* and in the world to come they shall be parted in every way, when he shall hide them in the hiding of his face from the disturbance of men.

*Peter.* The names of these men are fitting. Each ought to be Peter, that is, firm in faith. Then James, that is, the supplanter of vices. Then John, that is, one ascribing all things to divine grace against the pride of life, which is wont to arise out of the virtues.

*He was transfigured.* The form which he had by nature he showed, not losing the flesh which he had assumed by will. But that body which he had by nature he gave to his disciples at the supper, not mortal, not corruptible. *His face did shine.* As a pattern of the blessedness and brightness to come, which the just shall see, the wicked being first taken away. *And his garments,* etc. They were made white, which they were not before, because it hath not yet appeared what we shall be, but when it shall appear, we shall be like to him. Mark says, such as a fuller upon earth cannot make. That is, God cannot in this life make them so bright, because no one is without sin. No cleanser of himself upon earth will do what God does in heaven, cleansing his garment from every defilement. The fuller is a teacher of souls, or one who cleanses his own body.

*And behold.* Of what sort they were, or what they spoke, Luke says: *Seen in majesty, and they spoke of his decease which he was to accomplish in Jerusalem ((Luc. IX))*, that is, his passion and resurrection. They signify the oracles, etc., *as far as* that if Peter, seeing the humanity glorified, is affected with so great joy that he would never wish to be parted from the sight of it, what is to be thought of those who have deserved to see the Godhead.

*As he was yet speaking.* That he who sought a tabernacle may learn that in the resurrection they are to be sheltered not by the roof of houses, but by the grace of the Holy Spirit. *Behold a bright cloud,* etc. As when the Lord was baptized, so also when he was glorified the mystery of the holy Trinity is shown: because his glory, which in baptism we confess by believing, in the resurrection we shall praise by seeing. The Holy Spirit there in a dove, here in a bright cloud. Because he who now keeps the faith with a simple heart will then contemplate in open vision what he has believed, and will be sheltered by that grace by which he will be enlightened. *And behold a voice,* etc. Because he asked imprudently, he did not deserve an answer from the Lord: but the voice of the Father bears witness concerning the Son, and teaches Peter, and in him the rest, the truth. *This is the Son.* Moses and Elias are servants, and together with us they ought to prepare in their hearts a tabernacle for the Lord. *Hear ye him.* This the Father now enjoins, which Moses, giving testimony to the incarnation, foretold: *He shall raise up a prophet ((Deut. XVIII))*, etc. As if he said: This is he whom Moses promised.

*And the disciples hearing fell upon their face.* For they understood, higher than their sense, the one Godhead of both. They feared, either because they knew that they had erred, or because the cloud covered them, or because they heard the voice of the Father.
*Arise,* etc. Fear being driven off, doctrine is given, which while fear remained would not be heard.

*And lifting up their eyes,* etc. The cloud being taken away, they see Jesus, and that Moses and Elias had vanished: because after the shadow of the law and of the prophets departed, which had covered the apostles with its veil, the true light is found in the Gospel. *But only Jesus.* For if Moses and Elias had remained with Jesus, the voice of the Father would seem uncertain, to which of them it had rather given testimony.
*Tell it to no man unless,* etc. Lest the glory of the kingdom to come, being shown beforehand, should be past belief, and lest among the untaught the cross that followed should make a scandal.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Up the mountain his face began to shine.
Like the sun, his clothing white as light.
A bright cloud came and covered them.
And a voice spoke from the cloud.
This is my Son, the Beloved.
Listen to him.
Come, let us worship on the holy mountain.
We will listen to him. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Climb the mountain with the three of them, up out of the valley and into the high thin air, and watch his face catch fire with light.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
Moses is there, and Elijah, and Peter is babbling about building tents, wanting to hold the moment still.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
Then a bright cloud rolls over them the way it rolled over Sinai, and out of the cloud comes the voice.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
They fall on their faces, afraid — and he touches them and says, get up, do not be afraid; come down with me.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him. Amen.

lines: On the mountain his face shone like the sun.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
A bright cloud covered them, and a voice spoke.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
They fell down afraid; he touched them: rise.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him.
Come, let us worship on the holy mountain.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him. Amen.
